subject: english
topic: Spelling and punctuation: choose the correctly spelt/punctuated option

kept.q: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'the act of giving up a throne or position of power'.
options: Abdiccation
Abdication
Abdecation
Abdiccasion
kept.explanation: The correct word is 'abdication', formed from 'abdicate' plus the suffix '-ion'. The other options wrongly double the consonant, change the vowel or misspell the ending.
kept.pidgin: Na 'abdication' be the correct spelling, wey come from 'abdicate' join with '-ion'. Di other options just double wrong letter or spell am anyhow.

kept.q: In an examination hall in Minna, Fatima was asked to identify the correctly spelt word from a set that tests silent letters. Choose the correctly spelt word.
options: Pneumatic
Neumatic
Pnuematic
Pneumattic
kept.explanation: The word 'pneumatic' begins with a silent 'p' before 'n' and has one 't'. Candidates often drop the silent letter or wrongly double the final consonant, which the other options show.
kept.pidgin: Na 'pneumatic' correct because e get silent 'p' for front and one 't' for back. Di other options remove di silent 'p' or double letter where dem no suppose to.

kept.q: Choose the option that correctly uses the colon.
options: The coach named four players: Tunde, Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
The coach named: four players, Tunde, Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
The coach named four players, Tunde: Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
The coach named four players Tunde: Bisi, Kemi and Ngozi.
kept.explanation: A colon correctly introduces a list after a complete independent clause, as seen when it follows 'four players'. The other options place the colon in the middle of the clause or list, which breaks the grammar.
kept.pidgin: Na option A correct because colon suppose come after full sentence before you list something. Di other options put di colon for wrong place wey scatter grammar.

kept.q: Choose the correctly punctuated version of the following sentence: Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday however her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
options: Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday; however, her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday, however her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
Mrs Adebayo said that she would travel to Kano on Friday however, her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
Mrs Adebayo said, that she would travel to Kano on Friday; however her flight was later cancelled by the airline.
kept.explanation: Two independent clauses joined by the conjunctive adverb 'however' need a semicolon before it and a comma after it. The other options use only a comma before 'however', which creates a comma splice, or add an unnecessary comma elsewhere.
kept.pidgin: Na option A correct because when two strong sentence join with 'however', you must put semicolon before am and comma after am. Di other options make mistake with comma.

q.q: Choose the option in which the word is correctly spelt.
options: Embarrassment
Embarassment
Embarrasment
Imbarrassment
q.explanation: The correct spelling is 'embarrassment' with double r and double s. The other options wrongly drop one of the doubled letters or change the first vowel.

q.q: Choose the option in which all the words are correctly spelt.
options: Liaison, questionnaire, millennium
Liason, questionaire, millenium
Liaison, questionaire, millenium
Liason, questionnaire, millennium
q.explanation: All three words are correctly spelt only in one option: liaison, questionnaire and millennium. The distractors drop required doubled letters or misplace vowels in one or more of the words.

q.q: Choose the sentence that is correctly punctuated.
options: Adaeze, who scored 320 in UTME, gained admission to study Medicine.
Adaeze who scored 320 in UTME gained admission to study Medicine.
Adaeze, who scored 320 in UTME gained admission to study Medicine.
Adaeze who scored 320 in UTME, gained admission to study Medicine.
q.explanation: The non-defining relative clause 'who scored 320 in UTME' must be set off by a comma both before and after it. The other options miss one or both of the required commas.

q.q: Choose the option that is correctly punctuated.
options: The manager's report, which covered three quarters, showed that the company's profit had risen by 15%.
The managers report, which covered three quarter's, showed that the companys profit had risen by 15%.
The manager's report, which covered three quarters, showed that the companys' profit had risen by 15%.
The managers' report, which covered three quarters, showed that the company's profit had risen by 15%.
q.explanation: Only one option places the apostrophe correctly to show that the report belongs to a single manager and the profit belongs to a single company. The other options misuse or omit apostrophes on 'manager's' or 'company's', wrongly suggesting plural ownership or no ownership at all.
